article.headline: Neural Networks Think in Shapes; Goodfire Is Learning to Read Them
article.lede: Inside a language model, the concept of “Tuesday” is not stored as a label — the model bends its internal coordinate space into a loop, encoding the week as a circle. Goodfire, an AI interpretability startup, has launched a research series arguing that this **neural geometry** — the structured curves and surfaces hidden inside neural networks — is not incidental to how models work but constitutive of it. Mapping those shapes, the company contends, is the key to understanding and steering AI behavior with genuine precision.
article.body:
The animating insight is simple but consequential: **neural geometry** — the shapes that emerge when a network’s internal activations are plotted in high-dimensional space — is not an incidental byproduct of training. It is load-bearing. When a language model learns that Monday precedes Tuesday, it does not store that as an isolated fact; it bends its internal coordinate system into a loop, encoding the week as a circle. The same principle applies to months, to the color spectrum, to the topology of a map. *Gradient descent*, the optimization process by which networks learn, preserves the geometric structure of the world it absorbs.

Goodfire’s research team — led by chief scientist Tom McGrath, who founded the interpretability group at Google DeepMind (GOOGL), and including Atticus Geiger, Thomas Fel, and Ekdeep Singh Lubana — examined these structures directly in real models, including Llama 3.1 8B from Meta (META). The announcement’s accompanying image makes the finding visceral: Age, Temperature, Day, Year, Geography, and Colors each appear as distinct curved shapes extracted from the model’s *activation space* (the high-dimensional coordinate system formed by a network’s internal signals at a given layer). Days form a ring. Ages trace an open arc. Colors form a surface organized by hue, saturation, and lightness — reproducing, inside the model, geometry a physicist or painter would recognize from outside.

This creates real methodological friction. Two dominant tools in *mechanistic interpretability* — *sparse autoencoders* (SAEs), which decompose activations into human-readable features, and *linear steering vectors*, which nudge model behavior by adding a direction to its hidden states — both assume the relevant geometry is flat. SAEs, in Goodfire’s framing, “shatter manifolds into disconnected pieces,” capturing the atoms of meaning while losing the relational structure that connects them. Linear steering works adequately when a concept sits along a straight axis but misfires when the concept curves. Applying a flat vector to a circular representation is like navigating a winding road by pointing rigidly straight ahead.

Goodfire’s proposed remedy is *manifold steering*: rather than pushing activations in a straight line, the technique follows the *geodesic* — the shortest curved path — across the representation *manifold* (a lower-dimensional curved surface embedded in the larger activation space). The accompanying preprint (arXiv:2605.05115) shows that the activation manifold and the behavior manifold are approximately *isometric* — sharing the same geometric shape, correlated at r = 0.99 versus r = 0.36–0.89 for linear paths. In practice, manifold steering achieves 2.8 times lower cumulative output energy than linear steering and, in a days-of-the-week test on Llama 3.1, produces clean sequential day progressions where linear methods generate nonsense tokens.

Goodfire, founded in 2024 by Eric Ho, Dan Balsam, and McGrath, raised $150 million at a $1.25 billion valuation in February 2026, with Anthropic — whose own *Transformer Circuits* research program laid much of the conceptual groundwork here — among its backers. The commercial vehicle is Silico, a platform for inspecting and adjusting model behavior at the neuron level; the company reports using it to halve hallucination rates and to identify Alzheimer’s biomarkers from genomics models. The neural geometry series is the intellectual spine beneath those claims: if you can map the shapes inside a network, you can navigate them with precision.

concepts.definition: The structured shapes — loops, open curves, surfaces — that emerge when a neural network’s internal activations are plotted in high-dimensional space. Unlike a flat grid of independent features, neural geometry reflects the geometric organization of the world the model was trained on: cyclical concepts form rings, sequential ones form arcs, spatial ones form maps.

The core optimization algorithm used to train neural networks. Parameters are iteratively adjusted to reduce a loss function by moving in the direction of steepest descent on an error landscape. Because it is sensitive to the structure of training data, it implicitly encodes geometric regularities from the world into the model’s weights.

The high-dimensional vector space formed by all possible activation values at a given layer of a neural network. Each input to the network corresponds to a point in this space, and the geometric structure of that space — which points cluster together, which lie along curves — reveals how the network has organized its internal representations.

A subfield of AI safety research that attempts to understand what computations neural networks actually perform — at the level of individual neurons, circuits, and internal representations — rather than treating them as black boxes. The goal is to reverse-engineer the algorithms learned during training.

A neural network tool that learns to decompose a model’s activation vectors into a large dictionary of human-interpretable features, each of which is active for only a small fraction of inputs (hence “sparse”). Widely used in mechanistic interpretability to identify what concepts individual neurons or linear directions represent.

A technique for modifying a neural network’s behavior by adding a fixed direction vector — computed as the difference between two sets of activations — to its hidden states during inference. Sometimes called “representation engineering” or “activation addition.” Effective for concepts with flat geometry but unreliable when the concept’s representation is curved.

In mathematics, a shape that looks locally like flat Euclidean space but may be globally curved. A sphere is a two-dimensional manifold: any small patch appears flat, but the whole is round. Neural network activations are theorized to concentrate near lower-dimensional curved manifolds inside a much larger ambient space.

A proposed alternative to linear steering that moves activations along the curved surface of the representation manifold rather than in a straight line through ambient activation space. Uses geodesic paths rather than straight vectors, preserving the model’s natural representational geometry and producing more coherent behavioral changes.

The shortest path between two points on a curved surface. On a sphere, a geodesic is an arc of a great circle rather than a chord cutting through the interior. In the context of manifold steering, it is the path of least distortion through the curved representation manifold.

In geometry, two spaces are isometric if there is a distance-preserving mapping between them — they have identical shapes even if embedded in different surrounding spaces. Goodfire’s finding that the activation manifold and the behavior manifold are approximately isometric means changes to internal representations directly mirror changes in output behavior.

A research program developed primarily at Anthropic for mechanistically analyzing the internal algorithms of transformer-based neural networks. It reverse-engineers attention heads, MLP layers, and residual streams to understand what computations models actually perform. Published work covers induction heads, superposition, and the structure of features inside large language models.

article.fact_check: The quantitative claims — 2.8× output-energy reduction, r = 0.99 correlation between activation and behavior manifolds — derive from Goodfire’s own preprint (arXiv:2605.05115), which has not yet undergone independent peer review. The broader geometric observations about how concepts are organized in LLMs are well-supported by a growing body of academic work from groups at the University of Chicago, the University of Bristol, and Anthropic, making the foundational claims plausible even if the precise benchmarks await replication.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

ticker_meta.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
ticker_meta.blurb: Meta Platforms, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads — collectively the largest social-media ecosystem in the world by monthly active users. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue through digital advertising, using detailed behavioural data to target ads across its platforms. After a painful 2022 in which shares fell roughly 65% amid a revenue slowdown and ballooning metaverse losses, Meta executed a dramatic turnaround by cutting costs, boosting margins, and rapidly integrating AI-driven ad ranking tools (Advantage+) that demonstrably improved advertiser returns. CEO Mark Zuckerberg declared 2023 a 'Year of Efficiency' and the company followed through. By late 2025 Meta was simultaneously the most profitable it had ever been and the most aggressive in AI infrastructure spending, committing up to $65 billion in capex for 2025 and raising that figure to as much as $145 billion for 2026.
ticker_meta.recent: Meta reached an all-time high near $796 per share in September 2025. The stock declined approximately 24–28% from that peak through April 2026, with the primary investor concern being the scale of the 2026 capital-expenditure commitment — up to $145 billion — and uncertainty about whether AI-driven revenue would materialise at the pace required to justify it. Quarterly earnings remained strong through the period, but multiple compression drove share-price weakness.

poster_goodfireai.blurb: Goodfire is an AI research organization focused on mechanistic interpretability, neural geometry, and building tools to understand and control AI models. They post about their research agenda, including how neural networks represent concepts like time, space, and numbers along curved paths. Their platform Silico aims to enable building AI models with the precision of written software.
